key_insight: Truncating positional encodings breaks the theoretical equivalence seen in complete spectral and walk-based graph encodings, making different truncated families vary in expressive power.
engineering_relevance: For graph neural network design, this means the choice of truncated positional encoding matters materially for both model capability and performance, so mixing families can be better than relying on just one.
method: Analyze truncated spectral and walk-based positional encodings under graph expressivity theory.
Compare truncated families, including spectral PEs and k-harmonic distances, to show they are not equivalent.
Validate the practical impact with experiments on real-world datasets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports both theoretical results and experiments showing that a mix of truncated positional encodings outperforms any single family on real-world datasets.
watch_item: Truncated encodings reduce O(n^3) cost but can change expressive power substantially, so implementation choices like truncation level may alter model behavior in unexpected ways.
paper_title: Understanding Truncated Positional Encodings for Graph Neural Networks
